questions.question: In the following question, two statements are given each followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements. Statements: (I) Some white is black. (II) No black is green. Conclusion: (I) Some white is green. (II) Some white is not green.

questions.question: Directions: In a question below is given a statement followed by two inferences. Inference are logical conclusions from premises known or assumed to be true. You have to decide which inference can be formed from the given statement. Statement: "If you trouble me, I will slap you." - A mother warns her child. Inferences: I. With the warning, the mother might think that the child will stop troubling her. II. All children are naughty.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In a question below is given a statement followed by two inferences. Inference are logical conclusions from premises known or assumed to be true. You have to decide which inference can be formed from the given statement.

Statement: "If you trouble me, I will slap you." - A mother warns her child.

Inferences:

I. With the warning, the mother might think that the child will stop troubling her.

II. All children are naughty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1. Only I follows. Based on the given statement, inference - I follows but not II. The given statement tells that the mother is warning her child not to trouble her. So, if the statement is true, the first inference follows from the given statement i.e., the child will stop causing trouble because of the warning.

The statement is not sufficient to infer, in general, that all children are naughty.

questions.question: Find out the two signs to be interchanged to make the following equation correct. 13 + 26 × 2 – 5 ÷ 3 = 11
questions.questionHtml:
Find out the two signs to be interchanged to make the following equation correct.

13 + 26 × 2 – 5 ÷ 3 = 11
questions.solution:
A. – and ÷

Given expression: 13 + 26 × 2 – 5 ÷ 3 = 11

After interchanging the symbols, we get:

L.H.S = 13 + 26 × 2 - 53

= 13 + 10.4 – 3

= 23.4 – 3

= 20.4 ≠ R.H.S

B. × and ÷

Given expression: 13 + 26 × 2 – 5 ÷ 3 = 11

After interchanging the symbols, we get:

L.H.S = 13 + 26 ÷ 2 – 5 × 3

= 13 + 13 – 15

= 26 – 15

= 11 = R.H.S

C. + and –

Given expression: 13 + 26 × 2 – 5 ÷ 3 = 11

After interchanging the symbols, we get:

L.H.S = 13 - 26 × 2 + 5 ÷ 3

= 13 – 52 + 1.67

= 14.67 – 52

= -37.33 ≠ R.H.S

D. – and ×

Given expression: 13 + 26 × 2 – 5 ÷ 3 = 11

After interchanging the symbols, we get:

L.H.S = 13 + 26 - 2 × 5 ÷ 3

= 13 + 26 – 3.34

= 39 – 3.34

= 35.66 ≠ R.H.S

Hence, ‘× and ÷’ is the correct equation.

questions.question: Direction: A statement is followed by two courses of action numbered I and II. You are supposed to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement decide which of the suggested courses of action logically follow(s). Statement: The chairman stressed the need for making the education system more flexible and regretted that the curriculum has not been revised in keeping with the pace of the changes taking place. Course of Action I. Curriculum should be reviewed and revised periodically. II. System of education should be made more flexible.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: A statement is followed by two courses of action numbered I and II. You are supposed to assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement decide which of the suggested courses of action logically follow(s).

Statement: The chairman stressed the need for making the education system more flexible and regretted that the curriculum has not been revised in keeping with the pace of the changes taking place.

Course of Action

I. Curriculum should be reviewed and revised periodically.

II. System of education should be made more flexible.
questions.solution:
The logic followed is:

As the statement talks about the education system problem and the chairman stressed making it more flexible and regretted that the curriculum has not been revised in keeping with the pace of the changes taking place.

The statement speaks of inadequacies of the education system and emphasizes the need for flexibility and revision. Hence, both actions are the right courses of action to update the curriculum.

Hence, the correct answer is "I and II follow".

Additional Information

Some rules to solve Statements and Course of action questions must be kept in mind while solving it.

Rule 1. Have an unbiased and neutral mind frame. Individual perception must not be used to judge the course of action to be taken.

Rule 2. The first step should be to identify the root cause of the problem. Once the problem is solved, a logical mindset should be employed to figure out the course of action.

Rule 3. There must be no extremity involved in the course of action.

Rule 4. A course of action must be able to solve, reduce, or minimize the problem given in the situation.

Rule 5. The course of action can be said to solve/reduce the problem when it is an established fact, when it is logically possible and when it is known from experience.

questions.solution:
Given statement : 10 - 4 ÷ 20 + 16 × 8 = 16

According to the question, after interchanging of numbers and signs :

So,

  • Option - (1) : 10 and 16, × and ÷

16 - 4 × 20 + 10 ÷ 8 = 16

16 + 1.25 - 80 = 16

17.25 - 80 = 16

-62.75 ≠ 16 (LHS ≠ RHS)

  • Option - (2) : 4 and 8, × and -

10 × 8 ÷ 20 + 16 - 4 = 16

16 = 16 (LHS = RHS)

10 - 20 + 0.25 × 8 = 16

-8 ≠ 16 (LHS ≠ RHS)

20 - 4 ÷ 10 × 16 + 8 = 16

20 - 0.4 × 16 + 8 = 16

20 + 8 - 6.4 = 16

28 - 6.4 = 16

21.4 ≠ 16 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, "Option - (2)" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which two numbers (not digits) and two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1
questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers (not digits) and two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1
questions.solution:
Given equation: 18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1.

BODMAS Table: 

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) 3 and 30; × and +

Given: 18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1

After interchanging the numbers and signs we get;

⇒ 18 ÷ 30 - 3 × 15 + 2 = -1

⇒ 0.6 - 3 × 15 + 2 = -1

⇒ 0.6 - 45 + 2 = -1

⇒ 2.6 - 45 = -1

⇒ -42.4 ≠ -1

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 2 and 18; + and × 

Given: 18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1

After interchanging the numbers and signs we get;

⇒ 2 ÷ 3 - 30 × 15 + 18 = -1

⇒ 0.66 - 30 × 15 + 18 = -1

⇒ 0.66 - 450 + 18 = -1

⇒ 18.66 - 450 = -1

⇒ 431.34 ≠ -1

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 15 and 3; + and -

Given: 18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1

After interchanging the numbers and signs we get;

⇒ 18 ÷ 15 + 30 - 3 × 2 = -1

⇒ 1.2 + 30 - 3 × 2 = -1

⇒ 1.2 + 30 - 6 = -1

⇒ 31.2 - 6 = -1

⇒ 25.2 ≠ -1

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) 18 and 15; + and -

Given: 18 ÷ 3 - 30 + 15 × 2 = -1

After interchanging the numbers and signs we get;

⇒ 15 ÷ 3 + 30 - 18 × 2 = -1

⇒ 5 + 30 - 18 × 2 = -1

⇒ 5 + 30 - 36 = -1

⇒ 35 - 36 = -1

⇒ -1 = -1

⇒ LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits third to the left of D. D sits to the extreme right. Only two people sit between A and F. B is an immediate neighbour of F. Only one person sits between C and D. G is not an immediate neighbour of A. Who sits between B and A?
questions.questionHtml: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits third to the left of D. D sits to the extreme right. Only two people sit between A and F. B is an immediate neighbour of F. Only one person sits between C and D. G is not an immediate neighbour of A. Who sits between B and A?
questions.solution:
Given: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north.

1) D sits to the extreme right.

2) A sits third to the left of D.

3) Only two people sit between A and F.

4) B is an immediate neighbour of F.

5) Only one person sits between C and D.

6) G is not an immediate neighbour of A.

And, E will sit on the remaining place.

Here, "E" sits between B and A.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Statement : The taste of the coffee powder of the company X is better than the excessively advertised coffee of the company Y. Assumptions: I. If your product is not good, you spend more on advertising. II. Some people are tempted by advertising to buy a product.
questions.questionHtml:
Statement :

The taste of the coffee powder of the company X is better than the excessively advertised coffee of the company Y.

Assumptions:

I. If your product is not good, you spend more on advertising.

II. Some people are tempted by advertising to buy a product.

options.text: If only assumption I is embedded.
options.html: If only assumption I is embedded.

options.text: If only assumption II is embedded.
options.html: If only assumption II is embedded.

options.text: If either I or II is embedded.
options.html: If either I or II is embedded.

options.text: If both I and II are embedded.
options.html: If both I and II are embedded.

questions.solution:
I. If your product is not good, you spend more on advertising. → Not embedded

This assumption suggests a reason why company Y might spend more on advertising — to compensate for the inferior taste. The statement does not directly imply this, but it is a possible underlying reason.

II. Some people are tempted by advertising to buy a product. → Embedded

This assumption is implied directly because the statement mentions that company Y's coffee is much advertised, implying that advertising has an influence on consumer behavior.

Thus, only assumption II is embedded.

questions.question: Angle between hour hand and minute hand at 8:54 AM is:
questions.questionHtml: Angle between hour hand and minute hand at 8:54 AM is:
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:

The angle between the hour hand and the minute hand when the clock shows 8:54 AM can be calculated using the following formula:

Angle = [(11 / 2) M - 30 H]

Where, M = minutes and H = hours

Here, M = 54, H = 8.

Therefore, we get angle = (11 / 2 × 54 - 30 × 8).

297 - 240 = 57º

Hence, the correct answer is "57º".

questions.question: You are a police officer. A man complains that he has paid dowry to the in-laws of his daughter and that she is a victim of domestic violence. What will you do?
questions.questionHtml: You are a police officer. A man complains that he has paid dowry to the in-laws of his daughter and that she is a victim of domestic violence. What will you do?

options.text: Go and arrest the in-laws right away
options.html: Go and arrest the in-laws right away

options.text: Investigate and arrest the in-laws if deemed necessary
options.html: Investigate and arrest the in-laws if deemed necessary

options.text: Investigate and arrest the in-laws if deemed necessary, and frame charges against the man for paying dowry
options.html: Investigate and arrest the in-laws if deemed necessary, and frame charges against the man for paying dowry

options.text: Counsel the person and ask him to talk to his daughter's in-laws for a better future of her daughter
options.html: Counsel the person and ask him to talk to his daughter's in-laws for a better future of her daughter

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Investigate and arrest the in-laws if deemed necessary, and frame charges against the man for paying dowry.

Key Points

  • The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 prohibits both giving and taking dowry. Both acts are punishable under the law.
  • If a complaint of domestic violence is received, the police must conduct a fair and impartial investigation before taking action.
  • If the investigation reveals sufficient evidence, the police may arrest the accused persons in accordance with legal provisions and judicial guidelines.
  • Since the complainant admits to having paid dowry, the police are also duty-bound to initiate appropriate legal proceedings under the Dowry Prohibition Act, subject to the facts and evidence of the case.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate course of action is to investigate the matter, arrest the in-laws if necessary, and take legal action regarding the admitted payment of dowry.

Important Points

  • Giving, taking, or demanding dowry is prohibited under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
  • Domestic violence complaints require prompt investigation and appropriate legal action.
  • Police should follow the principles of fair investigation, due process, and applicable legal safeguards before making arrests.
  • For situational judgement questions, the best answer is generally the option that ensures both enforcement of the law and due process.
